description.narrative: The Project Development Objectives (PDO) are to improve resilient, sustainable, and safe road connectivity in rural areas of the Province of Guayas and, in case of an Eligible Crisis or Emergency, respond promptly and effectively to it.

The Project, requested by the Provincial Decentralized Autonomous Government of Guayas (PoG), aims to improve resilient, sustainable and safe road connectivity in rural areas of PoG and, in case of an Eligible Crisis or emergency, respond promptly and effectively to it.The PoG has prioritized road interventions based on the following criteria: (i) works to ensure connectivity between population centers, such as districts and parishes, prioritizing the areas most affected by flooding due to the effects of climate change; (ii) works with a large number of direct and indirect beneficiaries, especially those that promote the socioeconomic productive and tourist sectors of the communities to be benefited; (iii) works located on provincial boundaries that have not received attention to their needs on the last decade.The Project will comprise three components.Component 1 "Rural Road Construction and Rehabilitation (US$ 93.5 million)" includes rehabilitation of rural road; and reconstruction and construction of bridges in rural areas, aiming to enhance connectivity within the province. By strengthening infrastructure, the initiative aims to create a more resilient transportation network capable of withstanding environmental challenges. This Component is composed of 15 interventions, fully defined and agreed between the Borrower and the Bank during Project preparation. These intervention are detailed within the PAD and include seven roads (about 89.75 km) and eight bridges. All interventions will incorporate aspects of road safety audits recommendations, climate resilience, gender, and inclusion.Component 2 "Project Management and Capacity Building (US$ 6.5 million)" includes capacity building activities focused on supporting the PoG on managing the operation and increasing capacity for sustainable transport infrastructure management. Also, it includes cross-cutting subcomponents that will leverage the impacts of Component 1 by proactively engaging communities in Project design, monitoring and implementing approaches that will ensure social inclusion and protection, while contributing to increase participation and decision making, especially for women. These activities will embed the planning, design, construction, maintenance and social and environmental management of the rural state road network.Component 3 "Contingency Emergency Response (US$ 0 million)" is included under the Project in accordance with OP/BP 10.00, paragraphs 12 and 13, for situations of urgent need of assistance, as a Project specific CERC. Rural transport infrastructure is particularly vulnerable to climate disasters, including the CERC under the Project will allow for rapid reallocation of Project funds in the event of a natural disaster/ crisis during the Project's lifespan. Eligible emergency needs and the conditions to trigger this component will be specified in the CERC operations manual. This component will have no funding allocation initially and will draw resources from the unallocated expenditure category in the case of activation.

title.narrative: Road asset management system designed and operational with resilience and road safety considerations

comment.narrative: Bidding documents are currently being prepared for the “Provincial Road Infrastructure Strategic Plan,” which will include the development of an asset management system integrating resilience and road safety considerations. To support this process, the Bank has contracted an international consultant to advise the Province of Guayas. The bidding documents are in the final stages of review and are expected to be completed by the end of December 2025, with the tender anticipated to be launched in early 2026.

Guayas has informed the Bank of its intention to rehabilitate the following bridges:
• Cone (pedestrian): 55 m • Dolorosa (pedestrian): 75 m • Evia (vehicular): 25 m • Las Flores (vehicular): 25 m • Hediondo (vehicular): 20 m • Milagro (vehicular): 20 m • Limón (vehicular): 30 m • Toro (vehicular): 25 m
As the project advances, it will be reported which bridges are rehabilitated and which are reconstructed, noting that this will depend partly on the results of the resilience assessment being undertaken by the consulting firm.

Guayas has informed the Bank of its intention to rehabilitate the following roads:
• San Antonio – San Miguel: 7.5 km • Pedro VElez – Carlos Julio Arosemena: 16.79 km • Colimes – Olmedo: 29.13 km • Valle de la Virgen – Las Muras: 7.66 km and 5.20 km • El Deseo – Cruce Bueno: 5.05 km • Salitre – T de Baba: 5.91 km • Pauji: 3.50 km and 2.80 km
To date, no new roads are expected to be built. Reporting on this indicator will begin once rehabilitation works commence.

title.narrative: Women Certified in Heavy Machinery Operation

comment.narrative: On September 16, 2025, Guayas submitted a Gender Action Plan that includes training women in heavy-machinery operation. The ToR have been approved, and CONDU ESPOL will deliver the training. The contract is expected to be signed on December 22, 2025. The call for participants will be launched in January–February 2026. The first cohort (20 women, G license) will begin training on March 26, 2026, lasting four months. A second cohort (40 women—30 for G license and 10 for E license) will start on August 26, 2026; the E-license training will last eight months. As training progresses, the Project will report the number of women certified.

The Bank provided technical assistance to Guayas to develop a training plan for women on establishing micro-maintenance businesses. The consultant prepared a practical guide, supported by TF0C3494 (GFDRR), which was completed in November 2025. Guayas will lead implementation of the training outlined in the guide, aiming to support the creation of women-led microenterprises or increase women's participation in existing ones. Guayas has indicated that the plan will be prepared in early 2026, with implementation expected to begin in June 2026.

title.narrative: People benefiting from climate resilient infrastructure

comment.narrative: The project is in the early implementation stage. This indicator will be reported once the first climate-resilient works are completed and beneficiary estimates can be reliably calculated.

title.narrative: Direct users that benefit from improved access to sustainable transport infrastructure and services

comment.narrative: The project is still in its initial phase of implementation. Reporting on this indicator will begin once the first set of works is completed and the number of direct beneficiaries can be reliably estimated.

title.narrative: Complaints responded to and/or resolved within the stipulated standard for response times

comment.narrative: Guayas has established a Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM). This indicator will be updated as procurement advances and civil works begin. To date, no complaints have been received under the Project.

title.narrative: Recommended resilience measures included in the designs for the selected roads and bridges

comment.narrative: The resilience consultancy began on July 15, 2025. The firm will assess existing designs and conduct the necessary analyses to propose resilience measures for each intervention. The Borrower will review these recommendations and incorporate them into all interventions financed under the Project. As the consultancy advances, the Project will report the percentage of recommended measures that are ultimately adopted.

title.narrative: Share of roads and bridges rehabilitated where road safety audit recommendations have been implemented

comment.narrative: The road safety consultancy began on October 15, 2025. The consultant will review existing designs and carry out the required road safety audits to propose measures and recommendations for each intervention. These recommendations will be reviewed by the Borrower and incorporated into all project-financed works, as appropriate. Additional road safety audits will be conducted during construction and upon completion, prior to opening the roads to traffic. As the consultancy progresses and works advance, the Project will report the percentage of recommended measures that are ultimately adopted.

title.narrative: Civil works contractors trained in GBV risk prevention and mitigation

comment.narrative: This indicator measures the proportion of civil works contractors who receive training on GBV and SH prevention and response. Training will begin once civil works contracts are signed, and progress will be reported as contractors complete the required sessions.

title.narrative: Average travel time in areas of intervention

comment.narrative: The project is in the early implementation stage. This indicator will be reported once the first works are completed and travel time measurements can be reliably collected and validated.

title.narrative: Road traffic fatalities in areas of intervention

comment.narrative: The project is in the early implementation stage. This indicator will be reported once the first works, incorporating road safety audits and interventions, are completed and reliable road fatality data can be collected and validated.
